editorial:
Tony Montana arrives in Miami with nothing but ambition and a violent streak. After earning his green card through a bloody favor, he climbs the drug ladder fast, taking out rivals and building an empire built on cocaine and fear. Al Pacino plays Tony with wild energy, turning a ruthless criminal into someone you can't look away from. The movie is loud, flashy, and packed with memorable lines that have echoed through pop culture for decades.

The action hits hard, the pacing rarely slows, and the soundtrack keeps things moving from scene to scene. On the downside, the runtime is long and the violence is intense, so it's not for everyone. If you enjoy gritty crime stories with big personalities, this one delivers in spades.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Tony's paranoia peaks after he kills his best friend and his sister turns against him. A massive hit squad storms his mansion. Tony grabs a grenade launcher and fights back, killing many attackers, but he's overwhelmed. The last shot shows him falling into a fountain below, dead, with the famous globe statue behind him. His empire collapses instantly, proving his rise was as fast as his fall.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves gritty crime stories with big personalities.
